recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future Provenance/Event mismatch should be handled by a new, specific tracker rather than by applying the 2018 brainstormed element-name alternatives over later R5/R6 decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-13842 was a Published/Persuasive Security issue asking to align Provenance with the new Event pattern. The final resolution was to do the mapping, while the issue comment recorded that full Event alignment was not appropriate because Provenance has no independent lifecycle status and is not always about a subject.
initial_application: Git commit 7b2b64512052c9a800a59b0ac3cd2cd013659b1b explicitly lists GF#13842 and added a Workflow Mapping column plus Event mappings to the old Provenance spreadsheet source. That source was later converted into structuredefinition-Provenance.xml, where the workflow mapping identity and Event element mappings remain.
additional_context: Later Provenance/Event work refined the model rather than reversing the 2018 mapping. FHIR-28100 added basedOn and encounter, FHIR-38871 introduced pattern exception tooling, FHIR-42797 added Provenance.why, and FHIR-54833 confirmed the authorization element name/type and the role of Provenance.why for free text.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current build includes Provenance, the StructureDefinition declares the Workflow Pattern mapping identity, current elements map to Event root/occurrence/location/reason/code/subject/performer/function/actor, and provenance-event-mapping-exceptions.xml explains the intentional differences for subject, performer, reason, status, and statusReason.
